elements.quote: As the clinical course of patients with COVID-19 may widely vary across individuals, unexplored clinical parameters may explain this heterogeneity. Different definitions of the term 'severity' adopted by each author, some variables such as the time taken to collect laboratory tests or the number of the days from symptoms onset of COVID-19 to hospital admission may also have notably contributed to this circumstance. Discrepancies in reporting and detailing patients' comorbidities in each study may also have reinforced heterogeneity.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge regarding COVID-19 clinical course and the uncertainties/heterogeneity found in existing studies, which serves as the context for the review.

elements.quote: We believe that the results of our review and meta-analysis including a relevant number of patients, especially those related to IL-6 and ferritin, can be extrapolated to the real world, supporting clinical practice in coping with COVID-19 and may help decision-making processes.
elements.reason: The authors explain the importance of their review in supporting clinical practice and decision-making regarding COVID-19.
The manuscript does not indicate that this is an update or replication of a specific previous systematic review, so this conditional requirement does not apply.
This is a review of prognostic biomarkers (cytokine storm), not an intervention effect review; therefore, a mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.
This is not a review of complex interventions or delivery contexts; therefore, a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: To describe the laboratory parameters and biomarkers of the cytokine storm syndrome associated with severe and fatal COVID-19 cases.
elements.reason: The objective of the review is explicitly stated in the Abstract section.
This is a systematic review of observational studies (biomarkers/prognostic factors), not a review of intervention effects; therefore, PICO comparisons are not applicable.

elements.quote: Studies were included if they presented laboratory data-including serum IL-6 levels-from mild-to-moderate, severe or critical patients with COVID-19, according to the National Health Commission of China (NHCC) Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of COVID-19 [8] or World Health Organization Interim Guidance for COVID-19 [9]. Exclusion criteria consisted of studies that assessed pregnant women, pediatric patients, individuals co-infected with other microorganisms, or populations exclusively related to oncological, rheumatological, transplants, or chronic renal disease.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the inclusion criteria (laboratory data from COVID-19 patients) and exclusion criteria (specific populations like pregnant women, pediatric patients, etc.).
